syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Ganita Manjari PART-II
book.edition: NCERT (reprint year not stated in the prelims)

topics.title: Propositions and the converse of a proposition

concepts.learning_objective: State that a proposition is a statement that is either true or false.
Write the converse 'if Y then X' of a proposition of the form 'if X then Y'.
Recognise 'X implies Y' and 'Y when X' as other ways of saying 'if X then Y'.
Explain that a single counterexample is enough to show that a proposition is false.
Find counterexamples to claims that expressions such as Fermat numbers, 4n^2 + 1 or n^2 + n + 11 always give primes.

topics.title: Truth of a proposition compared with its converse

concepts.learning_objective: Show that a true proposition can have a false converse, using examples from numbers and daily life.
Give examples where a proposition and its converse are both true or both false.

topics.title: Perfect squares and an odd number of factors

concepts.learning_objective: Use factor-partner pairs to decide whether a number has an odd or an even number of factors.
Identify which of a proposition and its converse a chain of implications actually proves.

topics.title: Converses in geometry: the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem

concepts.learning_objective: State and apply the converse of the Baudhayana-Pythagoras theorem to decide whether a triangle is right-angled.
Judge the truth of converses of geometric propositions about lines and quadrilaterals.

topics.title: Divisibility and algebraic propositions and their converses

concepts.learning_objective: Decide whether converses of divisibility statements are true, giving counterexamples where needed.
Decide whether converses of statements such as 'if x = y then x^2 = y^2' are true for real numbers.
Explain why simply averaging the averages of groups of different sizes gives a wrong combined average.
Use (an + bm)/(n + m) to find the combined average of two collections of data.
Recognise that the average of averages is correct when all collections have the same size.
Calculate the concentration of a mixture as total quantity of the substance divided by total quantity of the mixture.
State the weighted mean formula and its history in the work of Brahmagupta and Sridharacharya.
Interpret weights as the relative importance given to each part of the data.
Compute a weighted score such as an annual mark or a combined rating from given weights.
Analyse how the weighted mean changes when all weights are scaled or increased by a constant.
Choose between cluster-column and stacked bar charts according to the comparison of interest.
Read totals, components and shares from a stacked bar chart.

topics.title: 100% stacked bar charts as an alternative to pie charts

concepts.learning_objective: Construct a 100% stacked bar chart by converting each component into a percentage of its bar's total.
Compare 100% stacked bar charts with pie charts as ways of showing proportions.
Decide which comparisons can and cannot be inferred from a 100% stacked bar chart.
Interpret charts that are both stacked and 100% stacked because every bar has the same total.
Describe an algorithm as a precise step-by-step procedure built from basic steps.
Execute and justify the right-to-left column addition algorithm with a carry.
Compare the effort of counting dots with the effort of adding column by column.

topics.title: Computing the divisors of a number

concepts.learning_objective: Execute the algorithm that builds the list of divisors of n by checking each j from 1 to n.
Use the pairing of divisors to reduce the numbers that must be examined.

topics.title: Finding the gcd from common divisors

concepts.learning_objective: Build the list of common divisors of two numbers from their lists of divisors.
Explain why the rightmost element of the common-divisors list is the gcd.

topics.title: Data structures and improving the gcd algorithm

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise a list as a data structure that stores named intermediate values.
Refine the gcd algorithm by combining scans, scanning up to min(m, n) and dropping lists.
Analyse how the work of the scanning gcd algorithm grows with the size of the numbers.
Justify that gcd(m, n) = gcd(n, m - n) when m is at least n.
Execute Euclid's subtraction algorithm, including the reversal and stopping steps.
Evaluate why the subtraction algorithm can need many steps for inputs like gcd(2k + 1, 2).

topics.title: Aryabhata's division algorithm and the history of the word

concepts.learning_objective: Use the reduction gcd(m, n) = gcd(n, m mod n) to compute a gcd in few steps.
Carry out the long-division layout for the gcd and read off the answer.
Recall how the word algorithm arose from Al-Khwarizmi and Indian arithmetic.
State the precise definition of a quadrilateral and recognise figures it excludes.
Identify vertices, sides, diagonals, adjacent and opposite parts, and valid names of a quadrilateral.
Decide whether a quadrilateral is convex using its internal angles or its diagonals.
Recognise non-convex, self-intersecting and non-planar 4-gons and where they arise.
Recall and justify the side, angle and diagonal properties of a parallelogram.
Use the converse tests and the equal parallel sides test to show a quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

topics.title: The Midpoint Theorem and its Converse

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the Midpoint Theorem to find lengths and parallel segments in a triangle.
Apply the converse of the Midpoint Theorem to locate midpoints.
Use the concurrence of medians and the 2 : 1 division at the centroid.
Show that the midpoints of the sides of any quadrilateral form a parallelogram and relate it to the diagonals.
Explain how copies of any quadrilateral can tile the plane.
Use the 360 degree angle condition at a vertex to decide whether a shape can tile.

topics.title: Linear equations in two variables and standard form

concepts.learning_objective: Identify a linear equation in two variables and write it in the standard form ax + by + c = 0.
Express an everyday situation as a linear equation in two variables.

topics.title: Solutions of a linear equation in two variables

concepts.learning_objective: Check whether an ordered pair satisfies a linear equation and recognise that there are infinitely many solutions.
Find the axis-intercept points of a line and relate solutions to points on its graph.
Explain why the line ax + by + c = 0 passes through the origin exactly when c = 0.
Calculate the slope of a line as rise over run using two points on it.
Read the slope and y-intercept from y = mx + d after rewriting ax + by + c = 0.
Recognise horizontal lines as having zero slope and vertical lines as having undefined slope.

topics.title: Pair of linear equations in two variables

concepts.learning_objective: Frame a pair of linear equations in two variables from a word situation.
State that a solution of a pair is an ordered pair satisfying both equations.
Solve a pair of linear equations by expressing one variable in terms of the other.
Solve a pair of linear equations by making coefficients equal and eliminating a variable.
Use the ratios a1/a2, b1/b2 and c1/c2 to decide whether a pair has a unique, no or infinitely many solutions.

topics.title: Graphical method for solving a pair of linear equations

concepts.learning_objective: Find the solution of a pair of equations as the point common to both lines.
Relate intersecting, parallel and coincident lines to unique, no and infinitely many solutions.

chapters.title: Math of Space: Surface Area and Volume

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the total surface area 2(lw + wh + hl) and volume lwh of a cuboid.
Use 6a² and a³ for the surface area and volume of a cube, including packing problems.
Compare solids of equal volume and reason about how surface area changes with shape.
Distinguish a right circular cylinder from an oblique one and describe its cross-sections.
Find the curved and total surface areas of a cylinder using 2πrh and 2πr(h + r).
Find and compare cylinder volumes using V = πr²h, including recasting and scaling problems.
Relate slant height, height and base radius of a right circular cone by l² = h² + r².
Find the curved and total surface areas of a cone using πrl and πr(l + r).
Use V = (1/3)πr²h, including solids formed by rotating a right triangle.
Describe a pyramidal shape as a base joined to a single apex in a different plane.
Find the volume of a pyramid as one third of base area times height.
Find the surface area of a pyramid by adding the areas of its faces.
Use 4πr² for the surface area of a sphere and relate it to the result of Archimedes about the enclosing cylinder.
Use V = (4/3)πr³ and reason about how volume scales with the radius.
Find the curved surface area 2πr², total surface area 3πr² and volume (2/3)πr³ of a hemisphere.

topics.title: Areas and volumes around us: guesstimates

concepts.learning_objective: Model everyday situations with solids and make reasoned estimates of quantities.
Explain why dividing volumes gives an upper bound when spheres are packed with gaps.
Convert volumes between cubic centimetres and litres using 1000 cm³ = 1 litre.
